items.title: Joel Dorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2007
items.q: And he distributed some of the independent records I had made with Duke Pearson and Sonny Stitt and people like that

ctx.x: Well I mean what is this — a business of — I mean Mother Theresa is not a record producer and doesn’t work at a record company you know, and neither did Bertrand Russell you know. We’re talking about you know like a few labels, a lot of acts, and you know, you’re like putting your money on different horses. So I had my group of guys that I wanted to do. Nesuhi, when he asked me to come to Atlantic full time to become the jazz producer it was because he had kind of run the string on his era. He had John Coltrane…
